newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IRI says it has eight offers for SEAT.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IRI says it has eight offers for SEAT.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding IRI said on Thursday it had received eight non-binding offers for SEAT, the publishing arm of state telecom holding Stet, and was now studying them.

IRI said in a statement that Lehman Brothers, the group's consultant, had received "eight non-binding preliminary offers from 21 individual bodies" for SEAT, which publishes the yellow page telephone directories in Italy.

"The consultant is in the process of examining the offers," the statement said, adding: "Lehman (Brothers) also specified that a total of 40 industrial and financial investors, both Italian and foreign, had shown interest in buying SEAT."
Last week, stock market watchdog Consob gave the go-ahead for the publication of a prospectus detailing SEAT's planned spinoff from Stet. Analysts believe SEAT to be worth more than $2 billion.
